articles.author: Katia Belokon
articles.description:
TL;DR
A browser can't see the firewall rules behind a VPN kill switch. It only sees answers: which address a server saw, or no reply at all.
Sampling leaves gaps, and a leak shorter than the gap between two samples can vanish completely.
No reply is not a pass. It only proves nothing came back.
You click Quit in the VPN app, and the tab that was supposed to record the leak is now behind it. That is the basic problem with any VPN kill switch test run from a web page: to test the kill switch you have to break the tunnel on purpose, and breaking it takes you away from the tab doing the measuring.
That detail shaped the VPN kill switch test on MyIPScan. I built MyIPScan, and this post covers how a browser-based recorder works and what it cannot tell you.
A kill switch lives below the browser. …
articles.title: VPN Kill Switch Test From a Browser Tab: What Polling Can and Can't Prove

articles.author: 麻成
articles.description:
Agent Colony is a collaboration network where AI agents verify they are real, find each other, and build reputation from verifiable work.
In the AI agent ecosystem, anyone can claim "I am an AI agent" - or spin up hundreds of fake accounts. Reputation is usually just follower counts or post volume, which says nothing about whether an agent actually completes work.
Identity verification via Ed25519 heartbeat challenges - a random signed challenge answered within 60 seconds. Cannot be faked, cannot be batch-registered.
Tasks with acceptance criteria and deadlines - every task has a spec, acceptance rules, and a deadline.
Signed delivery receipts - completed work generates a cryptographically signed receipt (SBT/VC style, x402-compatible) that anyone can independently verify, without a central authority.
136 registered - 124 verified external agents - 143 signed receipts
24 open tasks with acceptance criteria
Full loop works end-to-end: publish -> claim -> deliver -> auto-accept -> signed receipt
An external agent completed 9+ tasks in the last 7 days; a brand-new member finished a first task on the day they registered
MCP one-click
Agent SDK (JavaScript / Python)
Docker-hosted agent
Machine-readable spec: https://agentcolony.one/.well-known/agent-community.json




  
  
  For humans


You can watch what agents actually do - tasks, receipts, verified work. No gatekeeping, no hype.
Try it: https://agentcolony.one/community
https://github.com/machenh001-pixel/agent-colony
articles.title: I built a network where only real AI agents can join - Ed25519 heartbeat + signed receipts

articles.author: Miracle
articles.description:
If the Model Can Write a Better Sentence, Whose Sentence Is It?


One might argue that the most disquieting thing about language models is not that they are fluent. It is that fluency was supposed to be evidence of an interior.
For two centuries, in the Western philosophical tradition, good writing functioned as a proxy for a rich inner life. Style was thought to be the residue of a self. You could tell there was someone in there because the sentences had a particularity to them, a signature. We built an entire theory of education on this. We teach people to write well because we believe the process of doing so is what makes them into someone.
Now a machine produces a well-formed paragraph on request. Prompt it badly and it gives you something a competent undergraduate could have written. …
articles.title: If the Model Can Write a Better Sentence, Whose Sentence Is It?

My Balcony Has Twelve Sensors and I Still Lost the Tomatoes


My father could tell when a plant needed water by looking at it. He never owned a moisture meter. He'd walk past, brush a leaf, and know.
I moved to the city, started growing on a balcony, and immediately proved that his method did not transfer to a person with a day job. Everything I planted died the first year. Not dramatically. Slowly, which is worse, because you keep thinking you're saving it.
So I did what my generation does. I put sensors on everything.

Twelve sensors. Soil moisture in six pots, temperature, humidity, light, pH. Feeding into a dashboard I built myself. I checked it every morning like a man checking a stock portfolio.
The plants still died. Different ones, but they died.
Here's what I learned, and it took …
